Dust off the eyeliner and dig out those band tees — Emo Night just got a drag makeover and it's about to hurt so good. 🖤🎸 Sr. Knight Haven Rexia is hosting a full lineup of chaos: Beah Hazard, Moxie Mettles, Cherry Pop, Arakna Rexia Romanoff, and Ivy Rachael Mae are all bringing their angstiest, most theatrical looks to the Main Floor. Think teenage bedroom anthems, dramatic wig flips, and enough black lipstick to start a revival. This is the crossover you didn't know you needed — scene kid nostalgia meets full drag realness, one night only. Doors open early and this floor WILL fill up, so don't be the one stuck outside missing the first number. Grab your ticket now before Saturday sells out from under you. 🕷️🎤

Fog machine haze, guitar riffs bleeding into bass drops, and five queens who turned heartbreak anthems into full drag theater. 🌫️🎸 That's Emo Night: Drag Show Edition. Picture smudged black eyeliner catching the stage lights, green and pink wigs whipping through the air, spiked chokers glinting every time Beah Hazard, Moxie Mettles, Cherry Pop, Arakna Rexia Romanoff, and Ivy Rachael Mae hit their marks. Sr. Knight Haven Rexia keeps the room electric between numbers, and the Main Floor feels like your angstiest teenage diary come to life — but glammed up and turned all the way up. You'll feel the bass in your chest before the first look even hits the stage. This is nostalgia with claws, drama with a wig snatch, and a Saturday night you'll be replaying in your head for weeks. 🖤✨

Whoever you were at 15 — the one crying to your favorite album in a dark bedroom — she's invited too. 🖤🎧 Emo Night: Drag Show Edition isn't about looking a certain way, it's about feeling it. Band tees, fishnets, smeared eyeliner, or your Saturday best — walk in exactly as you are. Sr. Knight Haven Rexia hosts a lineup that gets it: Beah Hazard, Moxie Mettles, Cherry Pop, Arakna Rexia Romanoff, and Ivy Rachael Mae are turning teenage angst into full drag artistry, and the whole Main Floor becomes one big Latinx family screaming the words together. No judgment, no dress code police, just a room full of people who understand that emo never really left — it just found its glow-up. Come as you are, leave as part of the family. 🕸️👑
